title: When Jesus said, “Before Abraham was, I AM” (John 8:58), He wasn’t simply speaking about age or existence. He was declaring something far deeper—His eternal identity. Abraham lived nearly two thousand years before Jesus walked the earth, yet Jesus did not say, “I was before Abraham.” Instead, He used the sacred name “I AM,” the very name God revealed to Moses at the burning bush (Exodus 3:14). The people listening understood exactly what He meant. That is why they picked up stones. To them, this was either the boldest truth ever spoken—or blasphemy.
paragraphs: When Jesus said, “Before Abraham was, I AM” (John 8:58), He wasn’t simply speaking about age or existence. He was declaring something far deeper—His eternal identity. Abraham lived nearly two thousand years before Jesus walked the earth, yet Jesus did not say, “I was before Abraham.” Instead, He used the sacred name “I AM,” the very name God revealed to Moses at the burning bush (Exodus 3:14). The people listening understood exactly what He meant. That is why they picked up stones. To them, this was either the boldest truth ever spoken—or blasphemy.

This moment forces every person to confront the same question: Who is Jesus really? If His words are true, then He is not merely a teacher, prophet, or moral guide. He is the eternal God who stepped into human history. The carpenter from Nazareth is the Creator of the universe, the Alpha and the Omega.

This truth changes everything. If Jesus truly is the Great I AM, then His words carry eternal authority, His sacrifice carries eternal power, and His invitation carries eternal hope. The real question is no longer historical—it is personal. Do we recognize Him for who He truly is, and will we trust Him with our lives?
